OPERATING MODEL: 19 acceptance scenarios across 5 files (tests/security_rules/acceptance/sr01_define_and_redefine_rule.rs=5, sr02_signed_in_read_gated_by_rule.rs=5, sr03_anonymous_session_evaluated_as_null_auth.rs=3, sr04_untouched_collections_and_regression_suite_unaffected.rs=2 real + 1 structural marker (AC-17-16), sr05_simulate_rule_before_publish.rs=4) plus 12 layer-1 unit/property tests in crates/embyr-core/src/access_control/mod.rs (inline #[cfg(test)], 6 pinned examples + 2 proptest! blocks at 64 cases each, run via `cargo test -p embyr-core --lib access_control`). Per file, exactly one scenario is already enabled (not #[ignore]d) in source -- sr01/sr02/sr03/sr04's own walking-skeleton scenario (AC-17-01/06/11/14) plus, uniquely, sr05's own scenario 1 (AC-17-17's matching-pair case, enabled because it is that file's own chained Pillar-2 opening Given, even though US-05 is Release 2 and not tagged @walking_skeleton at the feature level) -- every other scenario is #[ignore]d with the literal string 'one-scenario-at-a-time RED discipline -- DELIVER unskips per step' (ADR-025 D2 discipline, ported from client-auth). For each step below, un-ignore the scenario(s) named in scenario_name ONE AT A TIME, then run that step's full test FILE (not just the one function) before committing -- sr01-05 all reuse an earlier scenario's Given/seeding shape within their own file (Pillar 2 chaining, documented in each scenario's own doc comment), so a regression there is cheap to catch immediately.

CRITICAL SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT -- CONFIRMED SATISFIED BY STEP 01-01: `SystemDb::get_access_rule` is wired UNCONDITIONALLY into `handle_get_document`'s new call site (crates/embyr-server/src/grpc/handler.rs:553-557, already real, non-scaffold code, confirmed by direct read during this roadmap's own preparation) -- a cheap existence-check against `access_rules` runs on EVERY GetDocument call, rule-defined or not, per ADR-029's own structural design. During RED this makes the pre-existing 113-scenario regression suite (72 embyr-rs + 41 client-auth) fail universally, independently confirmed by the orchestrator (`cargo test -p embyr-server --test us_03_read_document` panics inside `get_access_rule`) and documented in docs/feature/security-rules/distill/red-classification.md § Regression-Suite Finding. Step 01-01 (the ONLY step in this roadmap that touches a production .rs file) implements `SystemDb::get_access_rule` (ADR-028) such that a `(project_id, collection_path)` pair with no row returns `Ok(None)` -- at that point `handle_get_document`'s `rule_row == None` match arm (handler.rs:564-575) is EXACTLY today's pre-security-rules code, unmodified, and every one of the 113 regression scenarios (none of which seed an access_rules row) takes that identical branch. This restores the regression suite BEFORE rule DEFINITION (US-01's admin HTTP surface, step 02-01) or rule EVALUATION-when-a-rule-exists (US-02/03, steps 03-01/04-01) are separately verified against their own acceptance scenarios -- no step in this roadmap is sequenced before 01-01. Per the dispatch instructions' explicit direction, 01-01 implements ALL FOUR of this feature's scaffolded production functions together (embyr_core::access_control::{parse_condition,evaluate} ADR-027, AND SystemDb::{upsert_access_rule,get_access_rule} ADR-028) rather than a narrower 'get_access_rule-only' first increment -- this is a superset of the minimum the sequencing constraint requires, chosen because the dispatch instructions state this MUST land together in 01-01, and because (see FUNCTION-CALL DEPENDENCY TRACE below) these are the ONLY four RED-scaffold production functions in the entire feature -- there is no smaller meaningful increment that leaves any of the 4 unimplemented while still being useful to a later step.

FUNCTION-CALL DEPENDENCY TRACE (done before assignment, per this project's own established discipline -- traced against the actual scaffold markers in crates/embyr-core/src/access_control/mod.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/adapters/system_db.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/admin/handlers/access_rules.rs, and crates/embyr-server/src/grpc/handler.rs's handle_get_document, all read in full, not assumed from feature-delta.md's narrative alone): this feature's RED-scaffold surface is UNUSUALLY FLAT compared to client-auth's own roadmap. Exactly four production functions panic today -- embyr_core::access_control::{parse_condition, evaluate} and SystemDb::{upsert_access_rule, get_access_rule} -- and NOTHING ELSE. Confirmed by direct read: admin/handlers/access_rules.rs's define_access_rule and simulate_access_rule handlers are ALREADY real, non-scaffold code (session-auth, role-gate, project-ownership, request/response shaping, the SYNTAX_ERROR-vs-UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRUCT response-taxonomy mapping, the json_value_to_field_value translator) -- they call into the four scaffolds above but contain no scaffolded logic of their own, confirmed by their own module doc comment ('the session-auth / role-gate / project-ownership checks below are REAL, already-correct code ... only the two embyr_core::access_control calls and the two SystemDb calls they transitively reach are RED scaffolds'). grpc/handler.rs's handle_get_document extension (the get_access_rule lookup, the None short-circuit, the Some(rule_row) re-parse-and-evaluate branch including the EMPTY_FIELDS existence-non-leakage mechanism for AC-17-10) is likewise ALREADY real, wired code -- confirmed by direct read of lines 543-616 -- it calls the four scaffolds but adds no scaffolded logic of its own. migrations/0022_access_rules.sql is real, applied DDL, not a scaffold (confirmed present at repo-root migrations/, contra feature-delta.md's own path reference of crates/embyr-server/migrations/ -- this project's actual migration directory is workspace-root migrations/, verified by direct listing). tests/security_rules/common/mod.rs's SecurityRulesAdminContext/SecurityRulesFullContext and their seed_access_rule/seed_client_identity_credential/get_document helpers are likewise already real (they seed rows via raw SQL, bypassing the admin HTTP surface entirely for sr02/03/04/05's preconditions -- confirmed by direct read). CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: once 01-01 lands, EVERY remaining acceptance scenario in sr01-sr05 becomes a pure unskip-and-verify checkpoint against already-correct, already-wired production code -- no step after 01-01 in this roadmap modifies a production .rs file. This is confirmed, not assumed, by the trace above, and is stated explicitly in every downstream step's own implementation_notes so DELIVER does not go looking for production work that does not exist. Steps 02-01 through 06-01 (excluding 05-01's regression-proof half) therefore all list dependencies: ['01-01'] only -- 05-01 additionally depends on 02-01/03-01/04-01 purely for BUILD-ORDER reasons (the full regression re-proof is most meaningful once all of Release 1's individual story scenarios are independently confirmed green, mirroring the sequencing client-auth's own AC-16-08(a) discipline used), not because AC-17-15/16 have any additional PRODUCTION dependency beyond 01-01. 06-01 (US-05, Release 2) is independent of 02-01/03-01/04-01/05-01 -- confirmed by reading simulate_access_rule, which calls only parse_condition/evaluate (01-01), never get_access_rule/upsert_access_rule or any other story's own code path -- so 06-01 lists dependencies: ['01-01'] only, exactly mirroring client-auth's own verified-independent 02-02-depends-only-on-01-01 precedent.

STEP COUNT: 6 (01-01 through 06-01) mapping all 19 acceptance scenarios + the 1 structural marker (AC-17-16) with zero orphans and zero double-coverage: 01-01 owns the 4 canonical walking-skeleton scenarios (one per Slice 01-04, matching DISTILL's own WS Strategy section verbatim: 'four walking-skeleton scenarios, one per WS-tagged Slice'), 02-01 owns sr01's remaining 4 (AC-17-02..05), 03-01 owns sr02's remaining 4 (AC-17-07..10), 04-01 owns sr03's remaining 2 (AC-17-12..13), 05-01 owns sr04's remaining 1 real scenario (AC-17-15) plus the AC-17-16 regression-proof obligation, 06-01 owns all 4 of sr05 (AC-17-17 x2, AC-17-18, AC-17-19). 5+5+3+3+4 = 19 UAT scenarios (matches feature-delta.md's own DISCUSS count) with zero scenario name appearing in more than one step -- cross-checked function-name-by-function-name against all 5 acceptance files' actual contents, not assumed from the AC table alone. DECOMPOSITION RATIO CAVEAT (flagged explicitly, not silently exceeded): counting PRODUCTION .rs files only (2: crates/embyr-core/src/access_control/mod.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/adapters/system_db.rs), the ratio is 6 steps / 2 production files = 3.0, above this project's usual <=2.5 guidance (client-auth's own roadmap achieved 0.83). This is a deliberate, evidenced exception, not padding: per the FUNCTION-CALL DEPENDENCY TRACE above, this feature's entire production surface really is 4 functions in 2 files -- every one of the 19 acceptance scenarios still needs its OWN one-scenario-at-a-time RED-discipline unskip-and-verify checkpoint (mirroring this project's own ADR-025 D2 convention, already baked into every scenario's #[ignore] doc string) for traceability and to catch a regression the moment it is introduced, not because more production code needs writing per step. If counting ALL files touched (2 production + 5 test files touched exactly once each across steps 02-01..06-01), the ratio is 6/7 = 0.86, consistent with client-auth's own figure. Max scenarios in any single step is 4 (01-01/02-01/03-01/06-01, tied), well under the 8-scenario flag threshold this task's own dispatch instructions set.

GROUPING RATIONALE: (1) 01-01 is scoped to exactly the 4 canonical WS scenarios (not all of US-01's 5) specifically because DISTILL's own § WS Strategy section names these 4, and none of sr01's 4 remaining scenarios (redefine, the two grammar-rejection scenarios, the already-GREEN admin-auth scenario) are needed to restore the regression suite or prove the walking skeleton -- bundling them into 01-01 would blur the sequencing constraint's own 'sufficient to make the rule_row == None short-circuit path real' framing with unrelated US-01 completeness work, and would push 01-01 to 8 scenarios (the flag threshold) for no dependency-driven reason. (2) 02-01 through 04-01 are grouped strictly by user story (mirroring client-auth's own per-story phase boundary) even though the underlying production code is already 100% complete after 01-01 -- this preserves this feature's own AC/story traceability (each step's `acceptance_criteria` maps 1:1 to one DISCUSS user story's remaining ACs) and keeps each step's blast radius (one acceptance test FILE) obvious for review, matching the one-file-per-step precedent already established by sr01-sr05's own file-per-slice layout. (3) 05-01 bundles sr04's one remaining real scenario (AC-17-15, per-collection isolation) together with the AC-17-16 regression-proof obligation rather than giving the proof obligation its own step, because AC-17-16 is not an executable Rust assertion (the marker function `full_113_scenario_regression_suite_passes_unmodified` stays #[ignore]d PERMANENTLY, per its own doc comment -- 'DELIVER's own GREEN phase for this slice satisfies AC-17-16 by re-running the command below, not by unskipping and passing this function') -- it is a subprocess command DELIVER runs and records the result of, exactly mirroring client-auth's own AC-16-08(a) discipline, and belongs with the rest of US-04's own step for the same reason client-auth kept its own regression re-run embedded inside 02-02 rather than spinning out a dedicated step. (4) 06-01 is not split across sr05's 4 scenarios (unlike sr01/02) because 3 of the 4 are #[ignore]d together as one coherent US-05/AC-17-17..19 unit with no dependency ordering between them beyond the file's own already-enabled scenario 1, and splitting would produce a 1-2-1 scenario distribution with no story-boundary or dependency justification, unlike 02-01/03-01's clean per-story 4-scenario groupings.

PBT NOTE: 01-01 is this feature's ONE PBT-appropriate surface -- embyr_core::access_control::tests' 2 proptest! properties (64 cases each: any ownership condition against an empty resource map always denies [AC-17-09's generative form]; a mismatched-owner denial holds regardless of unrelated resource fields [AC-17-10's underlying mechanism, generative form]) -- already fully specified by DISTILL, not new test-authoring work for DELIVER, only implementation of the functions those tests exercise. This is this project's Hypothesis-equivalent per CLAUDE.md's functional-where-practical Rust paradigm (`proptest`, already a workspace dev-dependency, identical precedent to client-auth's own 01-01 PBT note). Every OTHER step (02-01 through 06-01) is layer-3 acceptance-level (real HTTP/gRPC + real testcontainers Postgres, verifying wiring through a real driving port, per the Two-Tier Acceptance Composition Decision already made during DISTILL: 'Tier A only, Tier B explicitly NOT added -- the entire condition-grammar input space is a small, closed, deliberately-capped set') and is EXEMPT per Mandate 9 -- each such step's implementation_notes states the exemption individually, matching client-auth's own per-step exemption-statement discipline. Mutation gate (per-feature, per project CLAUDE.md): `cargo-mutants -p embyr-core --filter access_control` targets 01-01's pure parse_condition/evaluate logic specifically (ADR-027's own Consequences section: 'mitigated by ... mutation testing (project's per-feature strategy, CLAUDE.md)'), run once 01-01 is GREEN -- before 02-01 begins, since every downstream step's correctness depends entirely on 01-01's two pure functions being genuinely correct, not merely test-passing.

EARNED TRUST NOTE: DESIGN (ADR-029 § Enforcement) already concluded, with explicit reasoning, that NO new probe() is required anywhere in this feature -- `get_access_rule`/`upsert_access_rule` execute through the existing, already-probed SystemDb connection pool (the identical substrate BC-1's own adapter methods already use), and `embyr_core::access_control::{evaluate,parse_condition}` are pure, deterministic CPU computation with no partial-trust surface, identical in kind and reasoning to `verify_client_identity_token()`'s own 'no new probe needed' justification (ADR-024, client-auth). This roadmap does not re-litigate that conclusion or add a probe() anywhere; no step below introduces a new driven adapter or new substrate dependency.

TDD_PHASES CONTRACT NOTE (orchestrator concern, recorded here per this task's own instruction): this project's DES stop-hook requires the literal legacy 5-phase names (PREPARE, RED_ACCEPTANCE, RED_UNIT, GREEN, COMMIT) in every crafter dispatch even though the actual work in steps 02-01 through 06-01 follows a degenerate form of the 3-phase ADR-025-equivalent canon -- for those 5 steps, RED_ACCEPTANCE is 'un-ignore the named scenario(s), observe it now compiles and its assertions are reachable against already-implemented production code', RED_UNIT is VACUOUS (no new unit-level production logic is added downstream of 01-01 -- see FUNCTION-CALL DEPENDENCY TRACE above), and GREEN is 'confirm the unskipped scenario(s) pass, with zero production-code edits' -- this is a legitimate, evidenced degenerate case of the phase sequence (comparable to sr01 scenario 5 / AC-17-05's own already-GREEN-by-construction status inside 02-01), not a shortcut being taken. Encoding the literal 5 phase names at dispatch time remains the orchestrator's own concern, not re-litigated here.

RELEASE GROUPING: phases 01-05 (steps 01-01, 02-01, 03-01, 04-01, 05-01) = Release 1 / Read-Path Protection Works End-to-End (US-01 through US-04) -- outcome: any collection Alex protects with a rule genuinely gates GetDocument reads by identity, for signed-in and anonymous callers alike, while every other collection and the full pre-existing 113-scenario suite remain provably unaffected. Phase 06 (step 06-01) = Release 2 / Authoring Confidence (US-05) -- outcome: Alex can prove a rule does what he intended before any real end user is affected by it. This mirrors feature-delta.md's own Release 1/Release 2 split exactly; no step crosses a release boundary.

phases.name: Walking Skeleton (US-01/US-02/US-03/US-04, Slices 01-04, Release 1) -- restores the 113-scenario regression suite

steps.name: Walking Skeleton -- embyr-core::access_control pure grammar + evaluator (parse_condition, evaluate, 12 unit/property tests, ADR-027) + SystemDb::{upsert_access_rule, get_access_rule} (ADR-028) -- the ONLY 4 RED-scaffold production functions in this feature; restores the pre-existing 113-scenario regression suite via the already-wired rule_row==None short-circuit in handle_get_document
criteria: parse_condition() accepts the locked v1 grammar (EBNF: condition:=or_expr; or_expr:=and_expr('||'and_expr)*; and_expr:=unary('&&'unary)*; unary:='!'unary|primary; primary:=comparison|'true'|'false'|'('condition')'; comparison:=operand('=='|'!=')operand; operand:='request.auth.uid'|'request.auth'|'null'|'resource.data.'IDENT) and returns a typed Condition AST (ADR-027)

parse_condition() rejects call-shaped syntax (get()/exists()) as ConditionParseError::UnsupportedConstruct{construct:CrossDocumentRead,..}, with a message naming cross-document reads specifically -- distinguishable from a generic ConditionParseError::SyntaxError for plain invalid syntax (unbalanced parens, unrecognized operator) (AC-17-03 vs AC-17-04)
evaluate() is total and infallible: EvaluationOutcome::Allow|Deny only, no panic, no Result in its return type -- AC-17-09's 'never crashes' claim is a type-level guarantee

evaluate(): Compare(AuthUid,Eq,ResourceField(_)) denies (fail-closed) when the referenced field is absent from resource_fields, or when auth is None -- the first FieldMissing anywhere in the condition tree collapses the WHOLE evaluation to Deny regardless of &&/||/! structure (ADR-027 Fail-Closed Semantics, AC-17-09)
evaluate(): Compare(AuthNullSentinel,Ne,NullLiteral) (the `request.auth != null` idiom) denies when auth is None and allows when auth is Some(_) -- the mechanism AC-17-11/AC-17-12 depend on
evaluate(): Condition::Literal(true) allows unconditionally regardless of auth or resource_fields contents -- the mechanism AC-17-12's public-read case depends on

All 12 layer-1 tests in crates/embyr-core/src/access_control/mod.rs::tests pass: 6 pinned examples (grammar acceptance x3, distinguishable-rejection x2, the 4-way evaluation truth table) + 2 proptest! properties at 64 cases each (`cargo test -p embyr-core --lib access_control` reports 12 passed, 0 failed)

SystemDb::upsert_access_rule(project_id, collection_path, condition_source) issues a single `INSERT INTO access_rules (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT (project_id, collection_path) DO UPDATE SET condition_source = EXCLUDED.condition_source, updated_at = now()` -- define and redefine are the identical SQL statement, no code branch distinguishes them (Resolution 3 / ADR-028)

SystemDb::get_access_rule(project_id, collection_path) returns Ok(None) for a (project_id, collection_path) pair with zero rows -- CRITICAL: this is what makes handle_get_document's existing rule_row==None branch (handler.rs:564-575, real code, unmodified by this feature) behave EXACTLY as pre-security-rules code for all 113 pre-existing regression scenarios, none of which ever seed an access_rules row

SystemDb::get_access_rule returns Ok(Some(AccessRuleRow{condition_source, created_at, updated_at})) for a seeded row, scoped strictly by the composite (project_id, collection_path) primary key -- a rule seeded for one collection is never returned for a sibling collection in the same project (the storage-level half of AC-17-15's isolation guarantee)

The 4 already-enabled (not #[ignore]d) walking-skeleton acceptance scenarios pass against real testcontainers Postgres, unmodified: sr01::first_time_rule_definition_succeeds_and_is_immediately_active (AC-17-01), sr02::a_signed_in_end_user_reading_their_own_document_succeeds_unchanged (AC-17-06), sr03::a_never_signed_in_session_is_denied_by_a_rule_requiring_identity (AC-17-11), sr04::a_collection_that_has_never_had_a_rule_defined_is_unaffected_by_this_feature (AC-17-14)

Regression restoration verified explicitly: `cargo test -p embyr-server --test us_03_read_document` (an existing, unmodified embyr-rs acceptance file that calls GetDocument, the exact file the orchestrator used to confirm the RED-scaffold panic) passes 4/4, with zero `SystemDb::get_access_rule -- RED scaffold` panics anywhere in the run
steps.implementation_notes: Replace both RED panics in crates/embyr-core/src/access_control/mod.rs (per DISTILL Scaffolds table: 12/12 unit/property tests panic unconditionally today; `cargo test -p embyr-core --lib access_control`: 12 failed, 0 passed). Types are already fully defined and real (Condition, Operand, CompareOp, AuthContext, EvaluationOutcome, ConditionParseError, UnsupportedConstruct) -- only the two function BODIES are scaffolded. parse_condition(source: &str) -> Result<Condition, ConditionParseError>: hand-rolled recursive-descent parser (ADR-027 Decision, zero new crate -- pest/nom were considered and rejected specifically because their extensibility is a liability against the locked, deliberately-closed grammar, ADR-027 § Considered Options). Tokenize, then parse via the EBNF in ADR-027 § Decision exactly (or_expr -> and_expr -> unary -> primary -> comparison), building the Condition/Operand enum tree the existing #[cfg(test)] block already pins via 3 example assertions (ownership_equality_condition_parses_into_a_compare_ast, null_auth_idiom_parses_into_a_compare_against_null_literal, bare_true_literal_parses_as_public_read). The tokenizer must specifically recognize `IDENT(` call-shaped syntax (mapping to UnsupportedConstruct{construct:CrossDocumentRead,...} per the cross_document_read_call_syntax_is_rejected_as_unsupported_not_syntax_error test) and any other named-out-of-grammar shape (custom function calls, `{...}`/`**` wildcard-path syntax -- CustomFunction/WildcardPath variants exist on UnsupportedConstruct for this, though no pinned unit test currently exercises them; implement the same call-shaped-syntax detection for both, since the acceptance-scenario coverage (sr01 AC-17-03) only exercises the get()/exists() case) BEFORE falling through to a generic SyntaxError for genuinely malformed input (unbalanced_parentheses_is_rejected_as_a_plain_syntax_error). evaluate(condition: &Condition, auth: Option<&AuthContext>, resource_fields: &BTreeMap<String, FieldValue>) -> EvaluationOutcome: recursive evaluation over the Condition tree. Represent field lookup internally as Result<&FieldValue, FieldMissing> (a private, module-local error type -- NOT ConditionParseError, which is parse-time only) so the first FieldMissing anywhere in the tree short-circuits the WHOLE evaluation to Deny (ADR-027 § Fail-Closed Semantics -- this is a deliberate simplification over per-operator null-propagation; do not invent per-operator semantics beyond what the 6 pinned examples + 2 proptest properties already specify). Comparison semantics per ADR-027 § Comparison Semantics: AuthUid vs ResourceField -- string-equality against auth.uid, Deny if auth is None or field missing; AuthNullSentinel/AuthUid vs NullLiteral -- the request.auth==null/!=null idiom, using auth.is_none()/is_some() (do NOT literally compare uid strings against a 'null' string -- NullLiteral is a distinct Operand variant, not a FieldValue); ResourceField vs BoolLiteral -- ordinary equality once the field is resolved (fails closed if absent, same mechanism); any other operand pairing accepted by the grammar falls through to ordinary FieldValue::PartialEq (already implemented, reused unchanged). And/Or/Not combine child evaluate() results with plain boolean logic -- Deny propagates through fail-closed the same way a false comparison would (do not special-case FieldMissing propagation through && vs || differently; ADR-027 explicitly rejects per-operator null semantics as unevidenced scope). Then replace both RED panics in crates/embyr-server/src/adapters/system_db.rs (AccessRuleRow struct is already real, non-scaffold). upsert_access_rule: `INSERT INTO access_rules (project_id, collection_path, condition_source) VALUES ($1, $2, $3) ON CONFLICT (project_id, collection_path) DO UPDATE SET condition_source = EXCLUDED.condition_source, updated_at = now()` against the real access_rules table (migrations/0022_access_rules.sql, already-applied real DDL at workspace-root migrations/ -- NOT crates/embyr-server/migrations/, confirmed by direct directory listing during this roadmap's own preparation, contra a stale path reference in feature-delta.md/ADR-028's own References section). get_access_rule: `SELECT condition_source, created_at, updated_at FROM access_rules WHERE project_id = $1 AND collection_path = $2` via sqlx::query_as, mapped through .fetch_optional(pool) so a zero-row result becomes Ok(None) naturally (do not special-case 'no rows' as an error -- CoreError should only surface for a genuine connection/query failure). CRITICAL: do not touch crates/embyr-server/src/grpc/handler.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/admin/handlers/access_rules.rs, crates/embyr-server/src/admin/router.rs, or any tests/security_rules/*.rs file in this step -- all are ALREADY real, wired, non-scaffold code (confirmed by direct read during this roadmap's preparation; see roadmap-level notes § FUNCTION-CALL DEPENDENCY TRACE) and require zero edits for the 4 WS scenarios or the regression suite to pass once this step's two files are correct. After GREEN, run the full sr01-sr05 suites with default #[ignore] filtering (`cargo test -p embyr-server --test security_rules_sr01_define_and_redefine_rule --test security_rules_sr02_signed_in_read_gated_by_rule --test security_rules_sr03_anonymous_session_evaluated_as_null_auth --test security_rules_sr04_untouched_collections_and_regression_suite_unaffected --test security_rules_sr05_simulate_rule_before_publish`) to confirm exactly the 5 already-enabled scenarios pass (4 WS + sr05's own chained scenario 1, AC-17-17, which becomes GREEN as a side effect of this step even though it is not owned by this step -- see roadmap-level notes § Grouping Rationale point 1; do not treat its early pass as license to skip 06-01's own explicit unskip-and-verify pass over it), then run `cargo test -p embyr-server --test us_03_read_document` to verify the regression-suite restoration claim directly. TEST PARADIGM (mandatory unless documented exempt): the 12 layer-1 tests in this step ARE this feature's property-based-test surface -- 2 proptest! properties (64 cases each) over the resource-field/uid input space, using Rust's `proptest` (this project's Hypothesis-equivalent, already a workspace dev-dependency per CLAUDE.md's functional-where-practical paradigm), already fully specified by DISTILL (no new test-authoring here, only implementation). The 4 acceptance scenarios in this same step remain layer-3/example-based and are EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: they verify real gRPC/HTTP + real Postgres wiring through a real driving port, not the pure grammar/evaluation invariants the proptest suite already covers directly. Mutation gate: run `cargo-mutants -p embyr-core --filter access_control` once this step is GREEN, before starting 02-01 (per-feature strategy, CLAUDE.md) -- every downstream step's correctness depends on these two functions being genuinely correct.
